picks.title: AI agents can form political camps—and changing their conversation partners does little to soften their views
picks.excerpt: In a Nature Communications experiment, LLM agents given political positions and free to choose their contacts split into opposing camps that increasingly preferred their own company; rewiring their partners did little to soften views.
picks.rationale: Multi-agent social-simulation slot: a Nature Communications experiment in which LLM agents that pick their own contacts split into polarized camps, and rewiring their partners did little to change that. The 10-25 Chalmers card measured the positions of single chatbots and the 10-21 card covered synthetic polling personas; this is a separate study about network dynamics among agents.

picks.title: SEEQC Combines Chip-Based Processing With NVIDIA AI to Improve Quantum Error Correction
picks.excerpt: SEEQC reports QEC decoding gains from a multi-stage architecture pairing its on-chip pre-decoder with NVIDIA's Ising open family of AI decoder models.
picks.rationale: Quantum slot: SEEQC reports a new result that pairs its on-chip pre-decoder with NVIDIA's open Ising AI decoders for error correction. The related 10-19 Riverlane card was about decoder calibration, a different company and a different step, so this is new.

picks.title: Researchers develop AI tool to map microRNA binding sites on circular RNAs
picks.excerpt: Pusan National University's circMAC predicts where microRNAs bind across full-length circular RNAs at single-nucleotide resolution, outperforming RNA language models in benchmarks (Briefings in Bioinformatics).
picks.rationale: Bioinformatics slot: circMAC predicts microRNA binding sites on full-length circRNAs at single-nucleotide resolution and beats RNA language models on benchmarks. It is basic RNA biology with no disease or patient involved, so it belongs in science, and it is not a protein or enzyme design story.

picks.title: App's AI 'eyes' for blind users fall short, researchers find
picks.excerpt: A study of blind users relying on AI visual-assistant apps for everyday tasks like cooking finds the AI descriptions often fall short, forcing repeated queries.
picks.rationale: Human-AI interaction slot: a field study finding that AI visual-assistant apps often fail blind users at everyday tasks such as cooking, so they have to ask again and again. The 10-05 visual-illusion card was about benchmark gaps in AI vision; this is a separate study of real-world use.

picks.title: Emergence of diffusion models from associative memory through memorization and generalization
picks.excerpt: Viewing diffusion models through Dense Associative Memory theory, the authors show that spurious states, long treated as memory errors, are a critical intermediate phase of generalization, and demonstrate them across many architectures and datasets.
picks.rationale: Science-of-AI slot: a new Nature Communications paper (10-25, the freshest item in the pool) that uses Dense Associative Memory theory to explain how diffusion models move from memorizing to generalizing, and finds that 'spurious states' are a necessary middle phase rather than errors. The nearest published card, the 10-14 MIT piece on how neural networks build their own learning machinery, is a different study on a different question.
